findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: There was no certified food protection manager present during today’s inspection. Another cook with a valid certification was supposed to be present but came late. Inspector was able to verify the certification validity.  Ensure that there is at least one certified food protection manager present at all times.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Steaks were observed being stored above fish and shrimp in the standing cooler on the far end of the wall right of the cook line. Education was carried out. The food items in the cooler were rearranged to be stored properly. Ensure that the appropriate storage order is followed to avoid cross contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The internal surfaces of the coffee makers in all the serving areas within the facility were observed soiled. PIC was made aware. PIC instructed employees to clean and sanitized them immediately while inspector was present. Ensure that food contact surfaces such as the coffee makers’ are monitored, cleaned, and sanitized at a regular frequency.

findings.title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
findings.comment:
There were no certified food protection manager with an active allergen awareness training certificate present and verifiable at the facility during today’s inspection. PIC did have one however, it had expired since 2021. PIC assured inspector that they would get the training done. Ensure that the training is done to be in compliant with the law.

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

findings.title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
findings.comment:
Repeat

A cook staff employee was observed handling fried foods on pass-through with bare hands. The fries and fried shrimp fell from the plate onto the pass-through surface, and the employee picked up the food items and placed them back on the plate with bare hands. PIC was informed of issue, and will re-educate staff. Ensure staff members are both handwashing and donning gloves prior to handling ready-to-eat (RTE) foods. A second follow-up will be conducted on 3/7/25 to ensure proper food handling is being conducted in the facility.
findings.citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT.

findings.title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
findings.comment: Observed staff member pick cooked broccoli up with bare hands that had fallen from bowl onto prep surface and place back in bowl. Observed staff member touch lobster and potatoes on plate with bare hands and serve plate. Observed staff member pick up garnish (kale) with bare hands and place on plate. Staff member was interrupted and asked to use gloves; staff member discarded garnish and donned gloves to finish the plate. Informed PIC that bare-handing ready-to-eat (RTE) foods is a direct threat to food-borne pathogen transmission. PIC will educate staff on proper food handling procedures and the importance of wearing gloves anytime they are handling RTE foods. A follow-up is scheduled for 3/4/25 to ensure staff are using gloves to handle RTE foods.
findings.citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed ice machines to be soiled with pink slime (mold) and debris. Mold is located on baffles and top of internal portion of ice machine. The machines are located behind prep area where bread is prepared. Informed PIC that ice machines need to be emptied and ice should be discarded before cleaning occurs. Mold and debris on the surfaces of the ice machine can contaminate ice, resulting in food-borne pathogen transmission.
findings.citation_text: 4-602.11(E) Equipment Food-Contact Surfaces and Utensils. (E) Except when dry cleaning methods are used as specified under § 4-603.11, surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting FOOD that is not TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be cleaned: (1) At any time when contamination may have occurred; (2) At least every 24 hours for iced tea dispensers and CONSUMER self service UTENSILS such as tongs, scoops, or ladles; (3) Before restocking CONSUMER self-service EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS such as condiment dispensers and display containers; and (4) In EQUIPMENT such as ice bins and BEVERAGE dispensing nozzles and enclosed components of EQUIPMENT such as ice makers, cooking oil storage tanks and distribution lines, BEVERAGE and syrup dispensing lines or tubes, coffee bean grinders, and water vending EQUIPMENT: (a) At a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or (b) Absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.

findings.title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
findings.comment:
2-401.11: Employee observed to have personal cup in kitchen at a food prep area. The cup was removed to a non food area. Ensure that personal drinks are in designated non food areas so that employees have to break from work to drink. This facilitates proper hand washing prior to the return to food service. 
(A) EMPLOYEE SHALL eat, drink, or use tobacco in designated areas away from FOOD and FOOD-RELATED areas. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEE may drink from closed BEVERAGE Container if handled to prevent: (1) hands (2) container (3) FOOD and FOOD-RELATED ITEMS.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: Fans in the kitchen have some dust and soil. Fans were taken down and washed. Fans move air through the kitchen, around food and items intended to be maintained clean, such as clean dishes. The violation was corrected immediately on site. Maintain fans clean to sight and touch. 
(A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
The facility has red sauce and ranch dressing date marked 3/26/24 in the walk in cooler. These items were discarded at time of inspection. The violation is considered corrected on site. The facility was closed for previous 4 days and is just reopening today. Ensure that foods do not extend past the 7 day date marking. Ensure to properly date mark all TCS foods.  The

3-501.18: (A) FOOD shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time criteria. (B) Refrigerated RTE TCS FOOD prepared in FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and dispensed through vending machine shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time.

6-201.16: (A) Wall and ceiling covering materials shall be attached so that they are EASILY CLEANABLE. There were personal drink cups on the table next to the employee pizza oven and a purse.  Develop a habit of placing personal items separate from items for the public. 

6-501.110: (A) Dressing rooms shall be used by EMPLOYEES if the EMPLOYEES regularly change their clothes in the establishment. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be used for the orderly storage of EMPLOYEE clothing and other possessions.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

Inspector observed the small dish machine to have 10ppm of available chlorine. The large heat sanitizing machine reads 162F. Do not use the small chemical machine and only use the large heat sanitizing machine until the small machine can be repaired. The repair technician has been called. The repair technician showed up and adjusted the machine to have 50ppm of available chlorine by replacing the squeeze tube. The violation has been corrected on site.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. 

Fans in the dish room are not running but are soiled with dust and dirt. Clean fan blades and wire covers before using them and maintain fans clean for next routine inspection.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Observed mold at several soda nozzles both in the main wait station and in the porch wait station. The soda nozzles were washed with soap and water, rinsed and sanitized with chlorine based sanitizer. Highly suggest the continued use chlorine to sanitize items with high sugar content in order to discourage mold. The violation is considered corrected on site. Maintain drink stations clean and sanitized.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. 

Observed the following areas in the facility to have accumulated soil:
1) The wall in the main wait station has red sauce splatter dried on it.
2) The floor to the left of the drink station in main is soiled and has some water on it.
3) The top of the ice bin at the drink station on the 2rd floor is soiled with soda spray.
4) The ceiling vent cover on the back side of the cook line has dust accumulated.
Clean and maintain the areas free of accumulated soil.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Observed the following food-contact surfaces and utensils to be in need of cleaning:
1. Soda nozzle holder at the bar had mold accumulation. Inspector showed PIC. PIC washed, rinsed, and sanitized the holder. 
2. Both ice machine baffles were soiled with pink, slime-y mold. Inspector showed PIC. PIC washed, rinsed, and sanitized.

Discussed routine cleaning of food-contact surfaces with PIC. Ensure staff is aware of the above listed places as frequent cleaning areas - wash, rinse, sanitize. COS.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-204.115: A WAREWASHING machine shall be equipped with a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE that indicates the temperature of the water: (A) In each wash and rinse tank; (B) As the water enters the hot water SANITIZING final rinse manifold or in the chemical SANITIZING solution tank. 

Observed no heat temperature test strips and/or a maximum registering thermometer in order to accurately measure the temperature of the dish machine. PIC ordered a maximum register thermometer during the inspection. Inspector will follow-up on 1/6/23.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

(REPEAT) Observed the following non-food contact areas in need of cleaning:
1. Baffles of the hood system have an accumulation of grease and debris.
2. Several reach-in coolers throughout the kitchen have dust on the interior fans. Repeat from 9/15/22 inspection.

Discussed routine cleaning of non-food contact surfaces with PIC. Ensure professional hood service regularly cleans the baffles and/or facility cleans themselves between services. Ensure staff is aware to routinely clean the fans within the reach-in coolers of dust.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-201.11: Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE.

2. Trim is missing from the corner of the heated dish machine area.

6. Server station hand sink downstairs needs re-caulked - coming away from sink and wall.
7. Caulk the wood platform by the small 3 compartment sink in the back server area of the kitchen (through the swing door near the reach-in coolers).
8. Re-caulk the hand washing station near the entrance to the prep area across from the walk-in freezer. 

#1-4 are repeat violations since the last routine inspection on 9/15/22. Discussed repairs with PIC. Ensure by next routine inspection.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-302.14: A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided. 

Observed no quaternary ammonium (sanitizer) test strips - QAC QR test strips. Facility has bounced back and forth between types of sanitizer utilized at the dispenser in the kitchen over the last two years. Previously was quaternary ammonium, then lactic acid, back to quat. Ensure facility has test strips to accurate test the sanitizer. Discussed with PIC. Inspector will follow-up on 9/27/22.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean

4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

6-201.11: Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.  

Observed many food handler’s licenses to be expired. Update the public health folder. Ensure all new hires have food handler’s within 30 days of employment. Keep copies at the facility. License is good for 3 years. Discussed with PIC.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
7-204.11: (A)-(B): Chemical SANITIZERS applied for FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall meet regulatory requirements. 

Observed the spray bottle of lactic acid to be too strong. Observed the lactic acid that is coming from the wall mounted dispenser to be too strong. Once the lactic acid was diluted with water, it was the appropriate concentration per the test strips. The product coming from the dispenser is 3010 ppm and turns yellow-green. Once diluted, the test strips were 1875 ppm and a darker green. PIC indicated that facility is likely going to be switching back to a more generic sanitizer - bleach or quaternary ammonium. Discussed with PIC that staff should be aware to dilute the lactic acid before placing in spray bottles. Discussed in-use rags and paper towels. Paper towels for the spray bottle; in-use rags for buckets of lactic acid. COS.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels. 

Observed in-use rags throughout the facility (bar and kitchen mainly). Discussed paper towel use for spray bottles of lactic acid. Discussed in-use rags for sani buckets of lactic acid. Keep rags in sani buckets with proper concentration of lactic acid. Change buckets of lactic acid as needed to stay between 704-1875 ppm. COS.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-302.13: (A) In manual WAREWASHING operations, a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be provided and readily accessible for frequently measuring the washing and SANITIZING temperatures. (B) In hot water mechanical WAREWASHING operations, an irreversible registering temperature indicator shall be provided and readily accessible for measuring the UTENSIL surface temperature. 

Observed no maximum registering thermometer and/or heat test strips for the heated dish machine. Discussed with PIC. PIC indicated he has a maximum registering thermometer at home. Inspector will follow-up on 3/25/22.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. 

(REPEAT) Observed the bar hand sink to be blocked by cocktail shaker, soap, and sanitizer product. Moved items to wash hands. Ensure all hand sinks are free and accessible at all times. COS. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 4/6/21 (blocked by ice then).

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
4-904.11: (A) cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed to prevent FOOD- and lip-contact surface contamination. (B) UTENSILS not prewrapped shall be presented so only handles are touched by EMPLOYEES and/or CONSUMERS. (C) SINGLE-SERVCIE ARTICLES intended for FOOD- and lip-contact shall be furnished for CONSUMER with wrapper or APPROVED dispenser. 

(REPEAT) Observed plates to be stored in a manner that allows for food- and lip-contact surfaces to become cross contaminated. Discussed inverting plates with PIC. Plates along prep line were observed to be displayed in multiple areas in this manner. PIC is aware and will cease practice. COS. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspections on 1/16/20 and 4/6/21.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
4-101.19: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other FOOD soiling or that require frequent cleaning shall be constructed of a CORROSION-RESISTANT, nonabsorbent, and SMOOTH material. 

(REPEAT) Observed both small chest freezers to have accumulation of ice and debris. Discussed routine cleaning with PIC. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 4/6/21.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-302.14: A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided. 

Observed no test strips for the peroxide cleaner being used as sanitizer. PIC called EcoLab. Test strips on order. Inspector will follow-up on 9/27/21.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. 

Observed many of the fans around the kitchen, ice dispenser area, and dish washing area to have accumulation of dust. 4-5 fans in total. Ensure routine cleaning of NonFOOD-contact surfaces.

(REPEAT) Observed dust within the fan in the reach-in cooler at the bar. Observed dust within the small reach-in cooler in the server area (contained condiments and shred cheese). Ensure routine cleaning of fans within coolers. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 4/6/21.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. 

Observed lack of caulk between the wall and the 3 compartment sink at the back server area. Caulk this sink to the wall before next routine inspection. Observed the back to-go order door to be missing a door frame and not sealed. Foam was visible. Seal this door.

(REPEAT) Observed upstairs server table top has paint coming away from the wood. Repair with paint to make smooth and easily cleanable. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 4/6/21.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
2-201.11: (A) The PERMIT HOLDER shall require FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES to report to the PERSON IN CHARGE information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD. Report: Symptoms (all P except lesion), diagnosis (all P), and possible exposures (P).  (E) Responsibility of food employee to report symptoms/disease to PIC. 

(REPEAT) Observed no signed employee health reporting agreements available for all food handler's at facility. PIC is aware and a copy was given. Inspector will follow-up on 4/16/21. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 1/16/20.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. 

Observed hand sink near side server area of main dining area to have ice within sink. Witnessed employee dump ice from personal drink within hand sink. Hand sink's are for hand washing only. Discussed with employee. Discussed with PIC. COS.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned. 

Observed ice cream scoops near bar to be immersed in water. Discussed ceasing practice with PIC. Created Time as a Public Health Control Policy for ice cream scoops. See attached in CDP. Ice cream scoops may be stored in room temperature water as long as scoops are washed, rinsed, and sanitized every 4 hours. COS.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
4-904.11: (A) cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed to prevent FOOD- and lip-contact surface contamination. (B) UTENSILS not prewrapped shall be presented so only handles are touched by EMPLOYEES and/or CONSUMERS. (C) SINGLE-SERVCIE ARTICLES intended for FOOD- and lip-contact shall be furnished for CONSUMER with wrapper or APPROVED dispenser.

(REPEAT) Observed plates to be stored in a manner that allows for food- and lip-contact surfaces to become cross contaminated. Discussed inverting plates with PIC. Plates near employee bathroom (bread warming area) and at prep line were observed to be displayed in this manner. PIC is aware and will cease practice. COS. This is a repeat violation from the last routine inspection on 1/16/20.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
4-101.19: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other FOOD soiling or that require frequent cleaning shall be constructed of a CORROSION-RESISTANT, nonabsorbent, and SMOOTH material. 

Observed chest freezer near back of prep line (contained onion rings) to have a large accumulation of frost. Discussed routine cleaning with PIC.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. 

(REPEAT) Observed the following areas to have accumulation of soil residues and debris:
1. Spray nozzle of 3 compartment sink/dish washing area has large amount of debris and grime on and under nozzle. This is a repeat violation since the last inspection on 1/16/20.
2. Walk-in cooler #2 (back of kitchen with majority of steak proteins) fan has dust accumulations.
3. Many reach-in coolers (mainly small reach-in coolers with condiments such as butter, blue cheese, cocktail sauce) have dust accumulation on the inside fans.

Wash, rinse, sanitized as needed throughout facility - specifically, the above mentioned places.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. 

Observed the following areas of the facility to be in need of repair and maintenance:
1. Paint inside cabinets of the server area near outside eating door. Interior of cabinets should be smooth and easily cleanable.
2. Upstairs server table top has paint coming away from the wood. Repair with paint to make smooth and easily cleanable.
3. Caulk the following areas: dish machine/3 compartment sink area and the prep sink area in the back (near walk-in cooler #1 and walk-in freezer).
4. Re-seal the door frame near the back of the kitchen by the server entrance door to the kitchen. Seal of door has been damaged and no longer there.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
6-403.11: (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use tobacco shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLESERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be located in a designated room or area where contamination of FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES cannot occur. 

Observed employee beverages within reach-in cooler of breading prep line area. Discussed designated storage area for employee drinks. PIC was in compliance. COS.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.citation_text:
2-102.11(C)(2) (Pf) PIC does not demonstrate the responsibility of preventing the transmission of foodborne disease by employees that may cause food borne disease. Discussed related section of the food code.  Reference 2-102.11(C)(2).

Observed facility to lack signed employee health reporting agreements. Provided additional copies of employee health reporting agreement, requirements for symptomatic employees for reporting (exclusion and restriction), and requirements for diagnosed food service employees. PIC stated he will have all employees sign document. Inspector will follow-up on 1/27/20.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-602.12  (C) Interior of microwave is heavily soiled. Interior cavity and door seals of microwaves must be cleaned and sanitized at least once every 24 hours. Reference 4-602.12.

Observed several microwaves to be soiled with debris. Discussed routine cleaning of microwave - wash, rinse, sanitize - during nightly cleaning. PIC was in compliance. Microwaves were cleaned during inspection. COS.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
4-903.11(A), (B) and (D)  (C) Clean Equipment/Utensils/Linens/Single-Use Articles stored incorrectly . Equipment, Utensils, Linens and Single-Use Articles shall be stored: 1) in a clean and dry location; 2) away or protected from contamination; 3) at least six inches above the floor; 4) covered or inverted. Reference 4-903.11(A), (B) and (D).

Observed several areas where plates were not protected from contamination (covered or inverted). Discussed proper storage with PIC.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text:
4-302.14  (Pf) Test kits or other devices are not available to the employees to measure sanitizing solution concentration. Provide a test kit or other measuring device so the employees can measure concentrations and ensure proper sanitization. Avoid a concentration of sanitizer that is too high, which can be toxic. Reference 4-302.14.

Observed facility to lack test strips and/or a maxiumum heat registering thermometer to measure heat at dish machine. PIC was made aware and will purchase. Inspector will follow-up on 1/27/2020.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text:
4-602.13  (C) Soil residue present on spray nozzle. Clean all non-food contact surfaces frequently to prevent soil accumulation.  Reference 4-602.13.

Observed heavy accumulation of debris on spray nozzle at 3 compartment sink. Discussed routine cleaning of nonfood-contact surfaces with PIC. COS.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.16  (C) Mop was found stored incorrectly in-between use. Mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, equipment, or supplies.  Reference 6-501.16.

Observed mop to be stored incorrectly in-between uses. Mops must be hung in a manner that allows to drip dry and/or air dry. Discussed proper mop storage in-between uses with PIC. COS.

findings.title: No bare hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed
findings.citation_text:
3-301.11 (P) Food employee used bare hands to handle ready to eat foods. Food employees shall use suitable utensils such as deli tissue, spatulas/tongs, dispensing equipment or single use gloves when handling ready to eat foods. Reference 3-301.11.

Observed bar staff slicing lemons without a barrier such as a glove. Food employees must utilize single use gloves to cut food that is ready-to-eat. Discussed with PIC. COS.

findings.title: Consumer advisory provided for raw/undercooked food
findings.comment:
Disclosure for consumer advisory for lightly cooked foods, such as steak and oysters, not provided at the time of inspection. Reminder statement was provided. Discussed menu changes with operator at the time of inspection. 
->A consumer advisory is not provided for serving raw or undercooked food. Discussed disclosure and reminder requirements. Consuming raw or undercooked meats, poultry, seafood, shellfish, or eggs may increase your risk of foodborne illness, especially if you have certain medical conditions. (Reference 3-603.11(A-C))

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Non-food contact surfaces found soiled at the time of inspection: Microwave near the hand sink at the end of the cookline found soiled with grime. 
->Thoroughly clean all cooking equipment and pans. (Reference 4-601.11(B-C))
